intro: Validation loss often fluctuates. Track meaningful improvements and stop only after a stated number of consecutive stalls.
task: Replay early stopping and return the best epoch, stopping epoch, and observed stall counts.
requirements: losses is a nonnegative vector in chronological order; patience is an integer 1..64; min_delta is nonnegative. Epoch indices start at zero.

Epoch zero initializes the best loss. Later improvement requires loss < best_loss - min_delta, strictly. An improvement resets the stall count; otherwise increment it. Stop at stall==patience and ignore subsequent losses.

Return {"best_epoch": integer, "stop_epoch": integer or -1 if no stop, "stall_counts": integer vector for processed epochs only}. The best epoch is the last meaningful improvement, not necessarily the smallest observed loss.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Stop after two stalls
examples.output:
{'best_epoch': 1, 'stop_epoch': 3, 'stall_counts': [0, 0, 1, 2]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Improvement resets patience
examples.output:
{'best_epoch': 4, 'stop_epoch': -1, 'stall_counts': [0, 1, 0, 1, 0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Minimum change boundary
examples.output:
{'best_epoch': 2, 'stop_epoch': -1, 'stall_counts': [0, 1, 0, 1]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Keep separate state for the remembered best loss and the consecutive stall count.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Equality at the min_delta boundary is a stall under this contract.

explanation: Patience tolerates isolated non-improving epochs while limiting repeated wasted evaluation. Remembering a meaningful best value lets several small improvements eventually exceed min_delta.

Stopping logic is a policy, so boundary conventions must be explicit. It uses validation observations and does not restore model parameters; the returned best epoch identifies which checkpoint a training loop should restore.
